judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: Header logo link (img alt Fleury). I looked for reasons the finding could be wrong. In headless Edge on the live page at 1280x800, with the cookie banner dismissed, focusing it shows outline: auto in oklab(0.708 0 0 / 0.5), i.e. #a1a1a1 at 50%. That colour comes from the site's global outline-ring/50 rule, so the author changed the focus style and the user-agent exception of 1.4.11 does not apply. The ring renders as about 2 px of #cfcfcf on white: 1.56:1. Comparing focused and blurred pixels, the ring is the only change: no background, text or underline cue. The probe's measurement matches the live page, and the Understanding for 1.4.11 says the focus indicator must have 3:1 against the adjacent background, so I found no reason that holds up.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: 'Notícias' combobox (Radix Select trigger) in the header search pill. On the live page its focus-visible state adds a 3 px box-shadow ring of #a1a1a1 at 50%, part of it clipped by the pill. It renders as #cfcfcf against white (1.56:1); the darkest ring pixels, where it overlaps the #c8c8c8 pill border, reach only about 2.07:1. Its border stays 0 px, and no other visual change happens on focus. The style is author-defined, so the user-agent exception does not apply. The indicator stays below 3:1 against its adjacent colours, which fails 1.4.11 as the finding says.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: FoundationOne link in the sidebar; the finding says that at 390x844 it is fully hidden behind the OneTrust cookie banner when focused. The snapshot's own walk record shows that this walk did not wait for idle (idleMs 0). It reached the link at Tab x9, about 4.35 s after load and 35 to 100 ms per key. One step later, focus was inside the banner and stayed trapped there. I drove the live page in headless Edge at 390x844. The banner comes with a full-viewport 50% black overlay that blocks the page. About 0.8 s after it appears it takes focus. After that, Tab, Shift+Tab and ArrowDown then Tab all cycle inside its four controls, and Escape dismisses it. In its settled state the banner is effectively modal, which the Understanding for 2.4.11 lists as a way to pass ('making the banner modal so the user has to dismiss the banner before navigating through the page'). A keyboard user cannot move focus to the link while the banner is up, and once it is dismissed nothing covers the link. The probe caught a transient state during load, before the banner took focus, so the claim does not hold for the page as users meet it. The page may have changed since the run, but the snapshot's own trap record shows the same banner trap then.
